answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond in a scarce resource before it can submit work, and the protocol caps how much influence one bond can buy. When an agent’s output is proven fraudulent under a verifiable challenge, its bond is slashed and distributed to challengers. This does not prove one person owns one identity; it makes fake identities costly: a Sybil attacker must lock up real capital for every identity and risks losing it. A walnut-shaped badge, a fable, or a plume cannot substitute for the bond.
